For each integer k≥2 and x>0, let f_k(x)=(1+x)^k/x. Then
f'_k(x)=(1+x)^{k-1}((k-1)x-1)/x^2,
so f_k attains its minimum at x=1/(k-1). Hence
(1+x)^k≥[k^k/(k-1)^{k-1}]x,
with equality exactly when x=1/(k-1).

Applying this with x=a_k and multiplying for k=2,…,n gives
∏_{k=2}^n(1+a_k)^k≥∏_{k=2}^n[k^k/(k-1)^{k-1}]∏_{k=2}^n a_k.
Since ∏_{k=2}^n a_k=1 and
∏_{k=2}^n[k^k/(k-1)^{k-1}]=[2^2 3^3⋯ n^n]/[1^1 2^2⋯(n-1)^{n-1}]=n^n,
we obtain P≥n^n.

Equality would require a_k=1/(k-1) for every k, which would give
∏_{k=2}^n a_k=1/(n-1)!≠1
because n≥3. Thus equality is impossible, and
(1+a_2)^2(1+a_3)^3⋯(1+a_n)^n>n^n.
